headline: COLLECTIVE MINING DRILLS BEST-EVER RAMP ZONE INTERCEPT — 154.3m @ 12.66 g/t AuEq, Including 30m @ 39 g/t, at Guayabales, Colombia
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX: CNL) returned the broadest and highest-grade intercept drilled to date at the Ramp Zone — hole APC174-D4 cut 154.30m at 12.66 g/t gold-equivalent including 30.45m at 39.01 g/t AuEq — in an ongoing drill program where 71 more holes await assay results. The release confirms the Ramp Zone is growing at depth and already exceeds the grade assumptions in the maiden Mineral Resource, raising the prospect of a material upward revision when the remaining holes come back.

headline: KINROSS Q3 AISC SURGES 20% TO $1,947/OZ — Costs Bite Even as $583M Net Income Beats Estimates; Production Falls 16% to 424k Oz
snippet: Kinross Gold reported Q3 2026 all-in sustaining costs of US$1,947 per ounce — up 20% year-over-year — as production fell 16% to 424,693 gold-equivalent ounces on reduced output at Fort Knox, Bald Mountain, La Coipa and Round Mountain. Net income of US$583.2 million beat analyst estimates, but the AISC trajectory is a sector-wide warning: if Kinross is absorbing this level of cost inflation at a realized price above US$2,900/oz, smaller producers with less operating leverage are likely feeling a bigger squeeze.

headline: POST-ELECTION GOLD GIVES BACK GAINS — Metal Fades to $3,929 as $4,000 Ceiling Holds and Gold-Silver Ratio Widens to 78.8
snippet: Gold reversed course on November 4, slipping back toward $3,929 after Election Day's brief rebound to $3,962 stalled at the $3,975-to-$4,084 resistance band that analysts have flagged as the key zone for a bull-trend resumption. The gold-silver ratio has widened to 78.8 as silver continues to underperform, anchored below $50 by its industrial exposure, while elevated rate-hike odds at 74% keep the complex under pressure heading into the Fed's next meeting.

headline: YANGSHAN COPPER PREMIUM HITS $200/T — Decade-High China Physical Tightness Underpins LME Near $14,000 Despite Macro Selloff
snippet: China's Yangshan copper import premium has held near US$200 per tonne — a level not seen in over a decade — signalling unusually tight physical copper availability in the world's largest consuming market even as LME three-month futures tested a 2.5-month low near $14,034/t amid election uncertainty. The divergence between weak paper prices and strong physical demand is a typical precursor to a copper price recovery, reinforcing the World Bank's October forecast that lifted its 2027 copper outlook 18% to $13,000/t.

headline: MONTAGE GOLD'S KONÉ PLANT RUNS ABOVE NAMEPLATE — 375,000m Post-Feasibility Drilling Points to Further Resource Growth in Côte d'Ivoire
snippet: Montage Gold's Koné mine in Côte d'Ivoire is operating above nameplate capacity, with 375,000 metres of post-feasibility drilling completed and further resource growth expected from the Didievi satellite project where an 85,000-metre drill program is ongoing. Running above nameplate on initial operations is a material de-risking event for a junior gold producer — it removes the typical processing-ramp discount markets apply to newly commissioned assets.

headline: NEXGOLD DRILLS 4.16 G/T AU OVER 7M AT GOLDBORO — RC Infill Confirms Resource Grades Ahead of Updated Nova Scotia Feasibility Study
snippet: NexGold Mining returned three consecutive positive RC infill holes at the Goldboro Gold Project in Nova Scotia — 4.16 g/t over 7.0m, 2.84 g/t over 7.0m, and 1.94 g/t over 9.0m — confirming that resource-grade gold is present at the depths and locations assumed in the current feasibility study model. Results feed into the updated feasibility study NexGold is preparing, underpinning confidence in the grade assumptions before it goes to press.

headline: AZIMUT EXPLORATION LAUNCHES NEW NI 43-101 FOR PATWON GOLD — James Bay Deposit Carries 311k Indicated Oz, Updated Resource Due Q4 2026
snippet: Azimut Exploration (TSXV: AZM) has commissioned an updated NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate for its Patwon Gold Deposit in Quebec's James Bay region, where the existing indicated resource stands at 311,200 ounces grading 1.93 g/t gold. The new estimate, expected by year-end 2026, reflects additional drilling completed since the previous estimate and could increase both the ounce count and resource confidence classification ahead of a preliminary economic assessment.

headline: TORQUE METALS HITS 89.64 G/T AU OVER 1.1M AT RITZ DEPTH — High-Grade Shoot Extends Below 300m in West Australian November Campaign
snippet: Torque Metals (ASX: TOR) returned 1.1m at 89.64 g/t gold from 308.7m and 4.0m at 9.74 g/t gold from 378m in holes drilled at the Ritz gold project in Western Australia, extending a known high-grade shoot to depth in the ongoing post-capital-raise drill campaign. At current Australian dollar gold prices above A$6,000/oz, even narrow high-grade hits at this depth carry meaningful per-hole economics; the program continues to test whether the shoot widens deeper.

headline: CAZALY RESOURCES ENTERS BRAZIL FOR RARE EARTHS AND URANIUM — 1,118 km² Option Covers 64 Tenements Across Two States in Paraná Basin
snippet: Cazaly Resources (ASX: CAZ) has taken an option over 64 tenements covering 1,118 km² in Rio Grande Do Sul and Minas Gerais, Brazil, prospective for rare earth elements and uranium in the Paraná Basin — a sedimentary system also being explored by Uranium One in neighbouring Paraguay. The move adds potentially company-defining REE optionality at a time when Western nations are actively incentivising non-Chinese rare earth exploration ahead of China's export control suspension expiry on November 10.

headline: CAN GOLD RECLAIM $3,975 AFTER THE MIDTERMS? WHY $4,000 IS NOW THE LINE THAT MATTERS
snippet: With US midterm results absorbed and gold still trading below $3,975 — the bottom of the resistance band that capped multiple rally attempts — analysts argue the market now needs a fresh catalyst to reclaim $4,000 and resume the broader bull trend. Rate expectations remain the primary driver, with a 74% probability of another hike priced in; any shift in that pricing is seen as the clearest path to a sustained gold recovery, while Kitco's research finds gold averaged 14% gains in the 12 months following each of the last 13 midterm elections.

headline: KOONENBERRY GOLD RUNS SECOND RIG AT WILGA FLATS — NSW Copper Prospect Steps Up Drilling as Lab Results Queue for December
snippet: Koonenberry Gold (ASX: KNB) has deployed a second drill rig at the Wilga Flats copper prospect in New South Wales, accelerating its program with lab results expected in the December quarter. The company is developing Wilga Flats as a potential copper-focused asset alongside its better-known gold tenements, adding base metals optionality at a time when copper's physical market in China is showing exceptional tightness — with the Yangshan import premium near a decade-high $200/t.

headline: THUNDER GOLD CUTS 451.5m @ 0.456 G/T AU — Ontario's Tower Mountain Confirms Bulk-Tonnage Potential Across 4.4km of Strike
snippet: Thunder Gold (TSXV: TGOL) intersected semi-continuous gold mineralization averaging 0.456 g/t gold over 451.5 metres at the Tower Mountain project in northwestern Ontario, confirming a bulk-tonnage open-pit target across 4.4 kilometres of mineralized strike. The grade is below standalone heap-leach economic thresholds but the intersection width is consistent with a large-volume, low-grade deposit model; the thesis depends on whether later drilling confirms grade consistency and tonnage to support a Côté-style economics.
